text: Iňačovce (Solymos, Ung county). Registers listed at the Prešov state archive: Greek Catholic 1811-1898, Reformed 1747-1940, Roman Catholic 1863-1926. The Greek Catholic run ends in 1898.
Iňačovce has been a Greek Catholic parish since the mid-18th century, per the Slovak public-administration portal's village profile.

FamilySearch catalogues Greek Catholic records of the Mukachevo eparchy for Ungvár / Užhorod and the Ung district, 1826-1938. Candidate home for the Maria Demko entry. Same item as the Duska agent's L-003.
Demko is a diminutive of Demeter / Dymitr / Demyan and occurs as a Polish, Slovak and Ukrainian/Rusyn surname. The name alone does not identify the family's origin.

A FamilySearch community thread: a researcher was told that registers for some Ung county places are missing from Prešov and went looking in Ukraine; the thread also says Ung county is absent from the 1869 census images on FamilySearch. Shows the Uzhhorod route is a known one for Slovak-side Ung villages.

Hungaricana urbarial tables for Solymos (Ung) list the landlords and their villein counts. Useful for placing a Demko household under a landlord if the family is found at Iňačovce in the 18th century.

Senné (Szenna, Ung) Roman Catholic register of births, marriages and deaths, 1831-1926, filmed from the Prešov state archive. Where a Duska-Demko marriage or their children's baptisms would be if the couple lived in Senné. Same item as the Duska agent's L-001.
Čičarovce (Csicser) was in Ung county and lies at about 48°33′N 22°02′E, south of Senné (48°40′N). Its register holdings were not retrieved in this pass.
Hungaricana urbarial tables exist for Csicser (Ung), listing seven landlords. A parallel table for Viszoka should be checked for a Demko villein.

Hungarian Act LIII of 1868, section 12: of the children of mixed marriages, sons follow the father's religion and daughters the mother's; contrary agreements are void. Text now sourced (DM-S-003-1, statute collection). Whether it was applied between the Roman and Greek rites is not settled; see ledger X-A-001.

Relayed, not seen: DUS:S-003 @53bf7f0. Later hand copy of a baptism, entry 13 of 1895: György, born 29 Mar, son of György Demko, Greek Catholic landholder, and Katalin Jobbágy, Gönyű (Gyňov) no. 24. Parish (Belža) from a folder name only. Coordinator crosswalk X-S-002.

Relayed, not seen: DUS:S-004 @53bf7f0. Later hand copy of a baptism, entry 33 of [1894]: Mária, daughter of József Hriczko, Greek Catholic, and Erzsébet Kocsis, Roman Catholic, Szina (Seňa) no. 182. A daughter of a mixed-rite couple in a book labelled Greek Catholic. The Duska agent holds Hriczko and Hreskó to be different surnames (DUS:H-017, 60). Crosswalk X-S-003.

Relayed from the Places agent, note to the coordinator of 11 Nov 2026: Vysoká nad Uhom is PL-P-037, 6.5 km from Senné and 9.3 km from Iňačovce, and was a Latin-rite filial of Pavlovce nad Uhom in a 1733 list (PL-S-010). Čičarovce is a different village further south and has a Greek Catholic parish today. The Places agent owns the question of which book the 1882 strip is from (X-Q-02, PL-H-008).

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Čičarovce village site, church page: Greek Catholic parish priests Jozef Kubek 1847-1881, then Ján Csurgovics 1882-1886. Roman Catholic priest Andrej (Endre) Polányi 1868-1890. In 1825 the Greek Catholic parish had twelve filials, among them Pavlovce nad Uhom, Vysoká nad Uhom and Vojany. All three confessions had a parish in the village.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Vysoká nad Uhom Greek Catholic parish history: a filial of Bežovce after 1771, of Čičarovce after 1806, a parish of its own only from 26 Sep 1948. Names a Ján Čurgovič among priests who served it.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. FamilySearch image groups for Čičarovce, via a finding list: Greek Catholic baptisms, marriages and deaths 1875-1886 on DGS 4406715 and 4406819; Roman Catholic baptisms filmed only for 1781-1849 (DGS 4405885). If the 1882 strip is a FamilySearch image, only the Greek Catholic book covers its year.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Parish geography: Greek Catholics of Senné, Jastrabie, Rebrín, Stretava and Stretavka belonged to the Greek Catholic parish of Iňačovce; Roman Catholics of Iňačovce, Palín, Stretava, Stretavka and Zemplínska Široká belonged to the Roman Catholic parish of Senné.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. A private transcription of the 1715 tax lists shows no Demko at Viszoka, Senné, Čičarovce or Iňačovce. The Viszoka list has a 'Joannes Heress', which may or may not be an early Hreskó.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Language and confession: Fényes (1851) describes Viszoka as Hungarian-Rusyn-Slovak with 331 Roman Catholics, 275 Greek Catholics and 182 Reformed, and Senné as Slovak-Rusyn-Hungarian. By 1910 Slovak was the recorded majority mother tongue in both.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Uzhhorod holdings: fond 151 of the Zakarpattia state archive is the board of the Mukachevo Greek Catholic eparchy. FamilySearch catalogue 1411329 films part of it; its inventories are catalogue 1411333, film 2376464 item 1. Whether it includes Čičarovce or Iňačovce was not checked.

As reported by the research pass DM-S-003-1; the page itself was not opened by this agent. Surname: Demko is a pet form of Demeter in Slovak and Polish use and of Demjan in Rusyn and Ukrainian use; Demkó is the same name in Hungarian spelling.

Places named in the Duska-repo strips and in folder F-02, flagged to the Places agent as written: Gönyű, Szina, Bölzse (Belža); Mogyorós; Tegenye; Pálócz; Bező; Lekárt; Vaján; a residence ending '-mező' (read as Feketemező by the Duska agent); Alsókánya; Magasrév.

From the Places agent @6eab2b2: Alsókánya is the Hungarian name of Jastrabie pri Michalovciach (PL-P-014), which the church books call Jesztreb. This confirms the reading 'Kelt: Alsókányán' in DM-D-008: the civil birth of 1906 at Solymos was registered at Jastrabie.

From the Places agent @6eab2b2: the Iňačovce Greek Catholic church archive was badly damaged by lightning on 6 July 1929 and by fire on 1 April 1930 (PL-S-046); the indexed register stops in 1898 (PL-R-003). Three birth volumes of a state register for 1895 to 1906 appear in an index of FamilySearch image groups (PL-S-047), not opened.

From the Places agent @6eab2b2: Greek Catholics living in Senné, Jastrabie and Stretava were registered at Iňačovce (PL-H-001, supported, 90). The Reformed of Iňačovce were a filial of Lúčky (PL-R-005). Vysoká nad Uhom stayed on the Slovak side in April 1939 (PL-S-036).

From the coordinator's method note of 12 Nov 2026 (ledger X-017): cholera waves in Hungary in 1831-32, 1848-49, 1854-55, 1866-67, 1872-73 and 1892-93. In this file: twins born in May 1873 both marked dead (DM-D-013), a first child dead at six weeks in February 1857 (DM-D-012). No cause of death is written on any strip in hand.
